reviewContext.userProblem: In session-471 the implementation-wave-outcome Opus step received about 8 MB of input and the provider returned 'Prompt is too long (~1.25M tokens)'. The session failed as adapterFailure, and --retry-failed-step resent the same input. Causes confirmed at 3f921eb4: (1) WorkflowFanoutChangeEvidence.reduce() emits one observation per (branch, capture record, drifted path) with no bound; (2) runtimeVariablesPrompt in composedPrompts renders the upstream payload three times (flattened top level, _rielaInput.messages[i].payload, _rielaInput.latest.payload); (3) nothing measures the composed request, and provider overflow is recorded as plain adapterFailure.
requiredOutcomes: changeEvidence.observations is aggregated per (branchId, selection, path), with occurrences, reasons and first/last stepId and snapshotPath. The inline list is capped by fanout.changeTracking.observationInlineLimit (default 200, range 0...10000). The join reports observationCount, observationOccurrenceCount, inlineObservationCount, observationsTruncated, observationsPath and observationCountsByBranch. The full list is written to <evidence dir>/observations.json. hasDrift is derived from the total count (pog-02).
A focused test with thousands of drifted paths across 3 branches keeps the serialized changeEvidence under 262144 bytes, with hasDrift and complete preserved (pog-02).

The runtime-variables block renders each message payload once, using the $rielaElidedKeys and $rielaSameAs markers. A runner test shows a 100 KB marker appears exactly once in systemPromptText + promptText. Templates still render from the original variables (pog-01).

A deterministic pre-invocation guard measures utf8(systemPromptText) + max(promptText, resumedPromptText) against payload.promptMaxBytes ?? defaults.agentPromptMaxBytes ?? 400000. When over budget it spills values of at least 4096 bytes to <workdir>/tmp/riela-prompt-spill/<sessionId>/<stepId>/<sha256>.json and replaces them with {$rielaSpilled, pointer, path, bytes, sha256, preview} stubs. It records inputSnapshot.promptCompaction and recomposes. If the prompt is still over budget, it records a failed step with failureKind promptTooLarge without calling the backend (pog-03).

WorkflowSessionFailureKind.promptTooLarge is added. adapterFailureKind(_:) classifies providerError/invalidInput messages that contain 'prompt is too long', 'context_length_exceeded', 'maximum context length' or 'request_too_large', and honors an explicit AdapterExecutionError.failureKind hint. It is applied at RuntimePublication.swift:348/:368 and DeterministicWorkflowRunner+Cancellation.swift:120 (pog-01).

The recovery gates (Recovery.swift retryableFailureKind, the SessionCommands retry guidance, DeterministicDirector rerunnable, TaskGuardCoordinator attempts-budget) treat promptTooLarge exactly like adapterFailure (pog-04).

An end-to-end runner test and a mock-scenario CLI run reproduce the session-471 shape: the join is bounded, the guard spills, and the agent step completes. A README section 'Agent prompt size limits' is added (pog-05).
arm64 swift build succeeds, the focused swift test filters pass with 0 failures, and swiftlint --strict passes on every Swift file changed since 3f921eb4 (tracked diff plus untracked new files).
nonGoals: No new retry or failure-transition route for failed agent steps; no rerunOnPromptTooLarge setting or director rule.
No compaction of node-authored payload.variables, memory guidance or output contract text.
No change to drift-detection semantics, capture/snapshot/manifest code, limits, drift reasons, artifactPaths, captureFailures, requiresSemanticReview or observationBoundary.
No AdapterExecutionErrorCode case; no GraphQL/SDL change (failureKind is already a String).
No committed example workflow or rielaExampleWorkflowNames() registration.
No push or merge (gitPush=false); workers run no git write commands.
constraints: Every build, test and lint runs as arch -arm64 /bin/zsh -lc. Use focused swift test filters; the full suite is not a gate.
Lint only Swift files changed since 3f921eb46e0a099b0d849adb62b8fb7ca69eb9af (tracked diff plus untracked new files). The 30 repo-wide diagnostics are an inherited baseline.
Scratch and evidence go only under tmp/prompt-overflow/<planId>/. Never mirror repository trees under evidence roots (fanout source snapshot cap is 512 entries).
Re-read each file before editing it and record pre/post sha256 per edit in that plan's own impl-plans/progress/<planId>.md; stop on drift; edit only the plan's own writePaths.

Spilled values are written under the run's working directory and referenced by path, bytes, sha256 and preview; they are never silently dropped. inputSnapshot.mergedVariables and adapterInput.mergedVariables are never compacted.
Runtime records stay owned by the runtime store; output is deterministic (no timestamps or UUIDs in spill files or stubs).
Encoded WorkflowDefaults, AgentNodePayload and WorkflowFanoutChangeTracking with the new fields unset are byte-identical to before.
designDecisionsAndRationale: Duplication is fixed inside the single runtime-variables block, not by dropping a channel: no adapter sends mergedVariables to a provider, and AgentGatewayNodeAdapter sends only systemPromptText and promptText (design Part B, Problem §2).
The dedup view is pure, sorted-key compactJSONString comparison. Templates keep reading the original variables, so existing prompts render unchanged (Part B).

Observations are aggregated by (branchId, selection, path) and sorted by plain String order for determinism. The full list is persisted with an O_EXCL/0600 pattern, and a persistence failure becomes a reduceFailures diagnostic with observationsPath null (Part A).

Spill selection takes the smallest candidate covering the excess, otherwise the largest, with ties broken by ascending RFC 6901 pointer. Candidates are re-enumerated on the compacted view each iteration; spill files are content-addressed (Part C).

The guard rejection is published through executeAndPublish after recordStepStartedExecution, not thrown, so exactly one failed step execution with promptCompaction evidence is recorded (Part D 'Guard rejection').
AdapterExecutionErrorCode stays closed; an optional failureKind hint on AdapterExecutionError plus a fixed-phrase classifier avoids altering a persisted closed enum (Part D).
promptTooLarge is a refinement of adapterFailure, so every existing recovery gate accepts it and no recovery path is lost (Part D 'Consumers of failureKind').
Shared contracts (failure kind, classifier, config fields, dedup view) are pinned in wave-1 pog-01 so wave-2 plans pog-02/03/04 have disjoint write sets.
intentionalTradeoffs: Every agent system prompt changes shape because of Part B dedup; agents keep full information through the markers.
Workflows whose prompts are above 400 KB start spilling; the spill is lossless and authors can raise promptMaxBytes or agentPromptMaxBytes.
Placed steps (step.placement != nil) are never spilled; over budget is an immediate rejection.
The 4096-byte spill minimum and 256-character preview are fixed constants.
Aggregated observation order changes from per-record order to sorted (branchId, selection, path).
supportedEdgeCases: observationInlineLimit 0: observations == [] while hasDrift stays true.
No drift: observationCount 0, hasDrift false, observations.json written with an empty list.
Repeated reduce() on the same actor replaces observations.json deterministically (rename preferred).
Unwritable evidence directory: a reduceFailures entry with path observations.json, complete false, observationsPath null, and inline observations kept.
Malformed or absent _rielaInput: the dedup view returns the input unchanged and never throws.
A message payload key overridden by a later message stays inline in the earlier message.
An existing spill file with identical bytes is reused; with different bytes it is a policyBlocked rejection recorded as a failed step.
A template interpolating a spilled value renders the stub JSON.
Retry after raising the budget: resume --retry-failed-step re-runs the guard with the current definition and completes.
timeout, policyBlocked, invalidOutput and templateResolutionFailed errors containing overflow phrases stay adapterFailure.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Token-level overflow when the byte budget is under the limit but the model's token window is smaller.
Which bytes to write when spilling a whole container whose shown form has duplicate keys removed (low residual risk).
Output-validation retry attempts reuse the guarded input without re-measuring it (low residual risk).
A failure-transition or retry route for promptTooLarge (open question, not requested).
